title: Herald Opens Its Howler Desk as Hogwarts Settles Into Peace
dek: A new paper for a rebuilt school: ink, parchment, and headlines that refuse to whisper.
body: With the castle's last scaffolding charms coming down, The Wizarding Herald begins publication from a cupboard that used to store brooms and now stores opinions.
Our promise is simple. If it happened at Hogwarts, in Hogsmeade, or in a Ministry lift that will not open, we will print it at a decent shout.
Subscriptions by owl. Complaints by Howler. We answer both.
author: Tobias Inkwood

title: Valentine's Post Sets New Record for Unsolicited Volume
dek: The Owlery has asked lovers to consider handwriting, or at least indoor voices.
body: February the fourteenth in 2006 produced a pink weather front above the Great Hall. It sang.
Percy-not-that-one Hobbs attempted to return a Howler. The Howler followed them to lunch and read itself between courses.
The Herald recommends flowers that do not talk. We sell none. We simply have standards.
author: Augusta Howl

title: New Charms Textbook Bites Three First-Years, Board Calls It Engaging
dek: Professor Vale issued plasters and a reading schedule that includes gloves.
body: The 2006 edition of Standard Book of Spells arrived hungry. Three first-years, including Alaric Pease, required plasters and a stern talking-to from the book.
Professor Vale said a lively text improves retention. The book said, and we quote, 'turn the page or else.'
The Board of Governors has called the edition 'engaging' and ordered more copies.
author: Minerva Quill

title: Herald Exclusive: Hogwarts To Relocate to the Owlery — Then It Didn't
dek: An April notice fooled three prefects, one governor, and briefly the ceiling.
body: A very official-looking notice announced that the castle would spend April in the Owlery 'for a change of air.' The stairs packed.
Felix Pennyworth arrived with luggage. Professor Bramble arrived with a counter-charm and a headache.
The Herald regrets the confusion and, in the same sentence, does not. Happy April.
author: Beatrix Crowe

title: Ravenclaw Study Group Invents Colour-Coded Howlers for Revision
dek: Red means 'you forgot the incantation.' Gold means 'you forgot to sleep.'
body: A Ravenclaw revision circle led by Otis Bramble enchanted leftover Howlers to shout only the bits of the syllabus they had missed.
Neighbours in the Room of Requirement reported improved scores and reduced peace. Hufflepuff students have filed a noise complaint written as an essay.
Professor Bramble confiscated the red ones and kept the gold ones. For research.
author: Minerva Quill

title: House Points Hourglass Drains Upward Overnight
dek: Gryffindor woke rich. Slytherin woke suspicious. The jewels refuse interviews.
body: Castle staff found the Gryffindor hourglass fuller than physics, magic, or grudges can explain.
Nell Vane called it 'overdue justice.' Slytherin prefects requested an independent jeweller.
The jewels, when asked, arranged themselves into the shape of a shrug.
author: Caspian Thorne

title: House Cup Heads to Ravenclaw After a Year of Loud Arithmetic
dek: Hufflepuff has requested a footnote. The jewels have requested a holiday.
body: End-of-term tallies in 2006 put Ravenclaw ahead, Hufflepuff close enough to sulk, and the hourglasses in need of a lie-down.
Cressida Pike was credited with the decisive batch of points for 'services to the Owlery.' The services remain classified and slightly sticky.
The cup will live in Ravenclaw common room until someone wobbles it again.
author: Gideon Fleet

title: Durmstrang Delegation Lost Between the Dungeons and Dinner
dek: They followed a staircase. The staircase had other plans.
body: A visiting party from the north spent two hours circling the dungeons after a staircase chose a scenic route through last century.
Professor Bramble found them by smell of fur cloaks. Cressida Pike offered a map that was, unfortunately, also from last century.
Dinner was held late. The visitors called the delay 'character-building' and asked for seconds.
author: Caspian Thorne

title: Start-of-Term Feast Opens 2006 With Sorting, Weather, and Warnings
dek: First-years found their houses. The ceiling found a new shade of drizzle. The Howler desk found work.
body: The 2006 term opened in the Great Hall with the usual miracles: the ceiling remembered the sky, the hats remembered the heads, and the staff remembered which end of the table is High.
Otis Bramble of Ravenclaw described the feast as 'louder than last year, which should not be possible.' Professor Amberly used the announcements to ban three charms that had not been invented yet.
The Herald's advice to first-years remains unchanged: follow a prefect, not a staircase.
author: Minerva Quill

title: First Full Post-Repair Term Begins Without a Missing Staircase
dek: Governors call it stability. Students call it suspicious.
body: For the first September in recent memory, every listed staircase was where the map said it would be. Several prefects checked twice.
Professor Vale told the Herald the castle is 'cooperating,' which in castle is a threat.
The Howler desk is nonetheless staffed. Peace is not the same as quiet.

title: Vanished Memos Found Filing Themselves in the Astronomy Tower
dek: The paper trail had legs. Then it had a union.
body: A stack of missing Board memos resurfaced in the Astronomy Tower, alphabetising themselves and hissing at anyone who said 'urgent.'
Felix Pennyworth tried to read one and was issued a receipt. Professor Quince tried to file one and was issued a warning.
Beatrix Crowe followed the trail to a cupboard that is now, officially, an archive.
author: Caspian Thorne

title: Halloween Feast Survives a Grindylow and a Self-Carving Pumpkin
dek: The bats were on time. The pudding was not. the Room of Requirement was briefly orange.
body: Halloween in 2006 delivered the traditional combination of delight and structural risk. A pumpkin in the Room of Requirement attempted autobiography.
Bram Oakley won the unofficial costume prize dressed as a Ministry decree. Professor Amberly deducted points for accuracy.
Ghosts reported the party 'adequately haunted.' The Herald takes this as a rave.
author: Tobias Inkwood

title: Enchanted Ceiling Over the Great Hall Forecasts Howlers
dek: Students now check the sky for both rain and incoming volume.
body: The ceiling above the Great Hall began displaying a new weather band this week: a crimson ribbon labelled HOWLER RISK.
Saffron Quinn said the ribbon turned scarlet whenever someone mentioned exams. Professor Amberly called the correlation 'statistically rude.'
The Herald recommends hats, ear-muffs, and a sense of humour.
author: Augusta Howl

title: Centaurs Object to Night Games Beside the Forest
dek: Astronomy homework, they argue, is not the same as a lantern festival.
body: A delegation from the Forbidden Forest asked Hogwarts to stop treating the tree line as the moving staircases after dark.
Mira Thistle was writing an essay by wand-light when a centaur inquired, politely, whether the stars had asked to be graded.
Professor Amberly has moved the class two lawns inward. The stars, so far, have not complained.
author: Seraphina Moon

title: Christmas at Hogwarts: Twelve Trees, One Argument, No Consensus
dek: Gryffindor wanted gold. Slytherin wanted green. The elves wanted everyone to sit down.
body: Holiday decorations went up over Honeydukes and immediately became a referendum on taste.
Isolde Crowe enchanted snow to fall upward. It was pretty until the owl post used it as a slide.
Those remaining for Christmas will receive extra pudding and a reminder that Howlers still work in December.
author: Rita Skeeter

title: House-Elves Vote on Pudding Policy After Cauldron Incident
dek: The 2006 pudding referendum was closer than the House Cup.
body: Kitchen staff called a snap vote after a cauldron of treacle tart developed ambitions and briefly occupied the dungeons.
Otis Bramble described the tart as 'aggressive but fair.' Professor Bramble confiscated spoons until further notice.
The elves have adopted a three-pudding maximum. Several ghosts have already filed a minority report.
author: Augusta Howl

title: Hogsmeade Station Adds Extra Owl for Sunday Returns
dek: Parents, parcels, and one very lost a Bowtruckle all tried to board the same carriage.
body: Weekend traffic in 2006 broke the unofficial record after Ravenclaw and Hufflepuff both booked the village on the same Saturday.
Nell Vane missed the train, posted themselves by owl, and arrived crumpled but on time.
The stationmaster has requested a second platform and a sense of proportion.
author: Elowen Proudfoot

title: Suit of Armour in the Black Lake Starts Unofficial Advice Column
dek: The armour is anonymous. The handwriting is not.
body: Notes signed 'A Friend in Steel' have appeared beside the Black Lake, offering counsel on homework, hexes, and whether Ravenclaw should sit nearer the potatoes.
Jonah Flint swears the advice saved a Transfiguration essay. Professor Vale swears the advice cited last year's exam.
The Herald will not name the armour. It asked us not to. Very politely. With a sword.
author: Augusta Howl

title: Ghosts Host Midnight Salon in the Moving Staircases

body: Nearly Headless Nick and friends held a salon to discuss castle politics, pudding, and whether 2007 has been 'too loud.'

Percy-not-that-one Hobbs missed the train, posted themselves by owl, and arrived crumpled but on time.
The stationmaster has requested a second platform and a sense of proportion.
author: Rita Skeeter

title: Start-of-Term Feast Opens 2009 With Sorting, Weather, and Warnings
dek: First-years found their houses. The ceiling found a new shade of drizzle. The Howler desk found work.
body: The 2009 term opened in the Great Hall with the usual miracles: the ceiling remembered the sky, the hats remembered the heads, and the staff remembered which end of the table is High.
Jonah Flint of Ravenclaw described the feast as 'louder than last year, which should not be possible.' Professor Vale used the announcements to ban three charms that had not been invented yet.
The Herald's advice to first-years remains unchanged: follow a prefect, not a staircase.
author: Minerva Quill

title: Vanished Memos Found Filing Themselves in the Astronomy Tower
dek: The paper trail had legs. Then it had a union.
body: A stack of missing Board memos resurfaced in the Astronomy Tower, alphabetising themselves and hissing at anyone who said 'urgent.'
Jonah Flint tried to read one and was issued a receipt. Professor Nightshade tried to file one and was issued a warning.
Beatrix Crowe followed the trail to a cupboard that is now, officially, an archive.
author: Caspian Thorne

title: Halloween Feast Survives a Kneazle and a Self-Carving Pumpkin
dek: The bats were on time. The pudding was not. Hogsmeade Station was briefly orange.
body: Halloween in 2009 delivered the traditional combination of delight and structural risk. A pumpkin in Hogsmeade Station attempted autobiography.
Mira Thistle won the unofficial costume prize dressed as a Ministry decree. Professor Bramble deducted points for accuracy.
Ghosts reported the party 'adequately haunted.' The Herald takes this as a rave.
author: Tobias Inkwood

title: House Points Hourglass Drains Upward Overnight
dek: Slytherin woke rich. Gryffindor woke suspicious. The jewels refuse interviews.
body: Castle staff found the Slytherin hourglass fuller than physics, magic, or grudges can explain.
Bram Oakley called it 'overdue justice.' Gryffindor prefects requested an independent jeweller.
The jewels, when asked, arranged themselves into the shape of a shrug.
author: Caspian Thorne

title: Ministry Owl Delivers 200 Howlers to the Wrong Tower
dek: A gale over the Black Lake turned official post into a public concert.
body: A Ministry dispatch owl lost its satchel over the Owlery on Thursday. Two hundred Howlers opened themselves in mid-air and read decrees to the lake.
Cressida Pike transcribed the loudest one, which concerned cauldron thickness. Professor Nightshade said the lake now knows more regulation than most seventh-years.
The Ministry has promised an inquiry and a quieter font.
author: Caspian Thorne

title: Christmas at Hogwarts: Twelve Trees, One Argument, No Consensus
dek: Gryffindor wanted gold. Slytherin wanted green. The elves wanted everyone to sit down.
body: Holiday decorations went up over Hogsmeade Station and immediately became a referendum on taste.
Tamsin Rook enchanted snow to fall upward. It was pretty until the owl post used it as a slide.
Those remaining for Christmas will receive extra pudding and a reminder that Howlers still work in December.
author: Rita Skeeter

title: House-Elves Vote on Pudding Policy After Cauldron Incident
dek: The 2010 pudding referendum was closer than the House Cup.
body: Kitchen staff called a snap vote after a cauldron of treacle tart developed ambitions and briefly occupied the Room of Requirement.
Nell Vane described the tart as 'aggressive but fair.' Professor Amberly confiscated spoons until further notice.
The elves have adopted a three-pudding maximum. Several ghosts have already filed a minority report.

title: Gryffindor Practice Halted After Bludger Develops Opinions
dek: A rogue Bludger spent forty minutes arguing with the Slytherin Beaters before vanishing into the Owlery.
body: Inter-house practice over the Owlery was suspended on Tuesday after a Bludger refused, in the words of Captain Isolde Crowe, 'to be hit in any direction that was not dramatically interesting.'

Professor Amberly inspected the ball and reported that someone had applied a commentary charm last updated in 2010. The charm offered live notes on every swing and rated the Gryffindor Chasers 'try-hard.'
The Department of Magical Games has asked for the Bludger to be sent to London. It left a forwarding owl.
author: Rita Skeeter

title: Herald Exclusive: Hogwarts To Relocate to the Forbidden Forest — Then It Didn't
dek: An April notice fooled three prefects, one governor, and briefly the ceiling.
body: A very official-looking notice announced that the castle would spend April in the Forbidden Forest 'for a change of air.' The stairs packed.
Felix Pennyworth arrived with luggage. Professor Vale arrived with a counter-charm and a headache.
The Herald regrets the confusion and, in the same sentence, does not. Happy April.
author: Beatrix Crowe

title: A Niffler Loose Near the Three Broomsticks After Care of Magical Creatures
dek: Nell Vane says it was a misunderstanding. The creature has retained counsel.
body: A practical lesson ended early when a niffler took a professional interest in the Three Broomsticks and would not be bribed with biscuits.
Professor Quince described the retrieval as 'mostly dignified.' Witnesses described it as a parade.
Nell Vane has been awarded house points for bravery and docked house points for providing a map.
author: Pandora Nettle

title: Astronomy Homework Claims Venus 'Refused to Cooperate'
dek: Professor Amberly accepted the excuse once. The planet has not issued a statement.
body: Third-year essays blamed Venus for incomplete charts after a cloudy week above the Great Hall.
Nell Vane submitted a drawing of a planet with its arms crossed. Professor Amberly wrote 'see me' and then, smaller, 'nice arms.'
Seraphina Moon notes that Venus is often uncooperative. That is why we like her.
author: Seraphina Moon

title: New Broom Trials Leave the Astronomy Tower Briefly Airborne
dek: A manufacturer demonstration in 2010 went well, then went up.
body: A visiting broom merchant demonstrated a 'whisper-quiet' model over the Astronomy Tower. It was not whisper-quiet. Several first-years reported their hats left without them.
Isolde Crowe completed three circuits before the braking charm remembered its job. Professor Nightshade called the landing 'educational.'
The merchant has offered Hogwarts a discount and a very long waiver.
author: Rita Skeeter

title: Centaurs Object to Night Games Beside the Forest
dek: Astronomy homework, they argue, is not the same as a lantern festival.
body: A delegation from the Forbidden Forest asked Hogwarts to stop treating the tree line as the Quidditch pitch after dark.
Saffron Quinn was writing an essay by wand-light when a centaur inquired, politely, whether the stars had asked to be graded.
Professor Nightshade has moved the class two lawns inward. The stars, so far, have not complained.
author: Pandora Nettle

title: House Cup Heads to Hufflepuff After a Year of Loud Arithmetic
dek: Ravenclaw has requested a footnote. The jewels have requested a holiday.
body: End-of-term tallies in 2010 put Hufflepuff ahead, Ravenclaw close enough to sulk, and the hourglasses in need of a lie-down.
Cressida Pike was credited with the decisive batch of points for 'services to the Quidditch pitch.' The services remain classified and slightly sticky.
The cup will live in Hufflepuff common room until someone wobbles it again.
author: Gideon Fleet

title: Suit of Armour in the Black Lake Starts Unofficial Advice Column

body: Notes signed 'A Friend in Steel' have appeared beside the Black Lake, offering counsel on homework, hexes, and whether Gryffindor should sit nearer the potatoes.

title: Decree 2011-B Bans Hovering Signage, Then Hovers
dek: The notice spent six hours arguing with itself above the Owlery.

body: A dozen exchange students arrived in 2011 expecting the Quidditch pitch to be picturesque rather than wet. It was both.
Felix Pennyworth ran an unofficial tour that began at the kitchens and ended, inevitably, at the Quidditch pitch.
Lucian Pips notes that the visitors' silk gloves have joined a house-elf sewing circle.
author: Caspian Thorne

title: Vanished Memos Found Filing Themselves in the Great Hall

title: Gryffindor Demands Recount After House Cup Goblet Wobbles

title: Moving Staircases Audit Finds Stairs That Prefer the Owlery

title: Snitch Hides in the Forbidden Forest Until After Curfew

body: Saturday's friendly between Hufflepuff and Ravenclaw ended in a draw after the Golden Snitch tucked itself behind a tapestry near the Forbidden Forest and went to sleep.

Gideon Fleet rates the match two brooms out of five, plus one extra broom for commitment.
author: Rita Skeeter

body: Halloween in 2020 delivered the traditional combination of delight and structural risk. A pumpkin in the Great Hall attempted autobiography.

dek: Hufflepuff wanted gold. Ravenclaw wanted green. The elves wanted everyone to sit down.
body: Holiday decorations went up over the moving staircases and immediately became a referendum on taste.
Saffron Quinn enchanted snow to fall upward. It was pretty until the owl post used it as a slide.
Those remaining for Christmas will receive extra pudding and a reminder that Howlers still work in December.
author: Rita Skeeter

title: Valentine's Post Sets New Record for Unsolicited Volume
dek: The Owlery has asked lovers to consider handwriting, or at least indoor voices.
body: February the fourteenth in 2024 produced a pink weather front above the Quidditch pitch. It sang.
Nell Vane attempted to return a Howler. The Howler followed them to lunch and read itself between courses.
The Herald recommends flowers that do not talk. We sell none. We simply have standards.
author: Augusta Howl

title: Level Two Lift Skips Hogwarts Liaison Again
dek: The liaison office has requested stairs. The stairs have requested hazard pay.
body: For the eleventh time this term, the Ministry lift refused to open on the Hogwarts liaison floor, depositing clerks instead near the Three Broomsticks in a painting.
Professor Quince received three clerks by Floo and sent them back with biscuits. Jonah Flint offered directions that led to the kitchens.
A memo promises 'improved wayfinding by 2024.' The memo is from 2024.
author: Beatrix Crowe

title: Herald Exclusive: Hogwarts To Relocate to Hogsmeade Station — Then It Didn't
dek: An April notice fooled three prefects, one governor, and briefly the ceiling.
body: A very official-looking notice announced that the castle would spend April in Hogsmeade Station 'for a change of air.' The stairs packed.
Otis Bramble arrived with luggage. Professor Kedgeree arrived with a counter-charm and a headache.
The Herald regrets the confusion and, in the same sentence, does not. Happy April.
author: Beatrix Crowe

title: House-Elves Vote on Pudding Policy After Cauldron Incident
dek: The 2024 pudding referendum was closer than the House Cup.
body: Kitchen staff called a snap vote after a cauldron of treacle tart developed ambitions and briefly occupied the Forbidden Forest.
Cressida Pike described the tart as 'aggressive but fair.' Professor Bramble confiscated spoons until further notice.
The elves have adopted a three-pudding maximum. Several ghosts have already filed a minority report.
author: Augusta Howl

title: House Cup Heads to Gryffindor After a Year of Loud Arithmetic
dek: Slytherin has requested a footnote. The jewels have requested a holiday.
body: End-of-term tallies in 2024 put Gryffindor ahead, Slytherin close enough to sulk, and the hourglasses in need of a lie-down.
Mira Thistle was credited with the decisive batch of points for 'services to the moving staircases.' The services remain classified and slightly sticky.
The cup will live in Gryffindor common room until someone wobbles it again.
author: Gideon Fleet

title: Gryffindor Seeks Fourth Consecutive House Cup, Pitch Already Nervous
dek: Slytherin has diagrams. Hufflepuff has snacks. Ravenclaw has a thesis.
body: If Gryffindor holds the cup again, it will be the longest run since the stands were rebuilt crooked.
Captain Saffron Quinn declined to predict a winner and then predicted a winner.
The jewels in the hourglasses have started leaning, which is not a recognised statistic, but we are watching.

body: A batch of career-guidance owls left London addressed to Howgwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. Three found a hill. One found us.
The Ministry blamed a helpful charm that 'corrects uncommon place-names.' Hogwarts is, famously, a common place-name.
The Herald will file Howgwarts as a search synonym and, if we are honest, as a house style for the letters page.
